name: Amos
bio:
Amos, a shepherd and sycamore-fig farmer from Tekoa in Judah, prophesied against Israel during the reigns of Uzziah of Judah and Jeroboam II of Israel, two years before an earthquake. He condemned the surrounding nations and Israel alike for their sins — oppression of the poor, dishonest trade, and empty religious ritual without justice — warning that Israel's prosperity would end in exile despite its confidence in its own strength and worship (Amos 1:1-6:14).

## 📖 Core Story: Confrontation at Bethel

After a series of visions of coming judgment, Amos's preaching at the royal sanctuary at Bethel provoked Amaziah, the priest there, who reported him to King Jeroboam as a conspirator and ordered him to leave and prophesy in Judah instead. Amos answered that he was no professional prophet but a shepherd whom the LORD had personally called, and pronounced judgment on Amaziah's own family for trying to silence God's word (Amos 7:1-17). The book closes with a promise that despite the coming devastation, God would ultimately restore the "fallen tent of David" and his people to their land, never to be uprooted again (Amos 9:1-15).
